theory.intro: A **forward scan** works left to right and gives each vertex its **earliest starting time (EST)**, the earliest all activities arriving there can be finished. A **backward scan** works right to left and gives each vertex its **latest starting time (LST)**.
facts: The start vertex always has an EST of $0$.
Going forward, add each activity's duration to the EST in the box at its tail vertex.
Where several activities arrive at one vertex, the EST is the **largest** of those totals.
The EST at the finish vertex is the minimum completion time for the whole project.
The finish vertex has an LST equal to its EST.
Going backward, subtract each activity's duration from the LST in the box at its head vertex.
Where several activities leave one vertex, the LST is the **smallest** of those results.
A dummy activity has duration $0$, so it passes a time across unchanged in both scans.
A correct pair of scans always leaves $0$ in both halves of the box at the start vertex.
steps: Draw a two-part box at every vertex
Set the start vertex EST to 0 and scan forward, taking the largest total at each vertex
Copy the finish vertex EST into its LST box
Scan backward, taking the smallest result at each vertex
